design:
D1. F1049 is decided in `scheduler.decide_firing`, not at the report site and not by a timer. Owner: `decide_firing`, because `FiringDecision` is the one answer to what a firing does and the board reads the same walk (`scheduler.py:2027-2040`). What happens today: the completion requests a firing 3 s later (`flow_advance.py:41`, `task_transition_service.py:979-980`); the fresh-review arm finds the author's turn still running and puts the task in `deferred` (`scheduler.py:2561-2570`); with no selection and nothing in flight the walk falls to `_stall_reason_from_walk`, which produces exactly F1049's two sentences, 'no claimable task among N open (1 completed)' or 'N still awaiting a prerequisite's approval' (`scheduler.py:3008-3022`); `_do_fire_job` writes a `skipped` run and reports `loop_stalled` (`scheduler.py:4400-4412`), whose new stall wakes the mender (`stalls.py:168-177`). `deferred` is documented as 'not an event, and not a stall' (`scheduler.py:2078-2082`), but the stall path never consults it. Decision: in that arm, record `(task.id, still_running)` in flight. The author's turn really is on the task: `task_attribution.attribute` will read it as `working` because a run with that `task_id` is running (`task_attribution.py:186-188`), and the existing F23 branch returns `DECISION_IN_FLIGHT`, which records nothing (`scheduler.py:4348-4364`). With no selections, `deferred` can only have come from this arm: the other two deferral sources need an agent already `taken` by this firing (`scheduler.py:2435-2443`, `1963-1971`, `2002-2021`), so no other stall shape changes. Rejected: 'seen on two consecutive firings'. It is timing-dependent (it hangs on the debounce and the tick spacing), delays every real stall by a full tick, and still leaves the board and the job history saying 'stalled' for a flow that is working. Rejected: suppressing only `stalls.report` when `deferred` is non-empty, which fixes the wake but leaves the false `skipped` row and board label.

D2. Safety of D1: the gap is closed by the author's run ending, which calls `flow_advance.after_run` (`agent_trigger.py:3745`, `4781`; `flow_advance.py:70-80`) and fires the flow; that firing offers the review (`test_review_waits_for_the_authors_turn.py:60-74`). A run that never ends is still caught by the sweep: `dead_run` when this Hub is not executing it (`stalls.py:700-717`), and `no_progress` after 30 minutes without a run start or a transition (`stalls.py:746-788`). Neither reads `decide_firing`.

D3. The mender's questions are notes always, not only while the operator is away. No presence signal exists: `Project.last_seen_at` is written only when a project's directory is observed (`project_lifecycle.py:520-525`), and the grep for `operator_activity|presence|operator_away|last_active` finds no operator signal. Building one is a product concept of its own, and slice D owns windows. A note answered while the operator is present costs one extra mender turn (the answer is queued as input, `questions.py:594-613`) in place of a turn held open for up to 240 s. Owner: the Hub, at `api/v1/agent_actions.py`'s two question routes, so a model that passes `blocking: true` cannot override it; `_record_the_wait_and_park` already skips non-blocking questions (`agent_actions.py:844-858`), so no wait is stamped and no task parked. The tool decides whether to wait from its own argument (`mcp_server.py:574`), so it must also read the Hub's record: it returns at once when no row came back blocking. That is general (the Hub's record decides), not a mender special case in the tool. The mender ends the stall `gave_up` naming the note; F1048's rule (`stalls.py:202-224`) then counts further reports of the same reason on that stall without waking anyone. No new outcome is added.

D4. Where the answer goes. `deliver_batch_if_complete` puts every delivered answer in the asker's latest open conversation (`questions.py:164`). For the mender, which holds one open conversation per stall (`stalls.py:493-508`), that can be another stall's thread. Since F804 each question records the conversation it was asked in (`schemas/questions.py:80-84`), so delivery prefers that conversation when it is open and belongs to the asker, and falls back as today. This is general, not mender-only: answering in the thread a question came from is what F804's per-conversation tray already promises.

D5. 'Sonnet by default' is the catalog default, decided when the mender is resolved. Owner: `stalls.ensure_mender`, the one place the mender's runner is chosen (`stalls.py:406-467`, called on every wake and when the entry is turned on, `api/v1/manager.py:94-101`). Today an empty `ManagerJob.model` means the chosen runner's model (`stalls.py:421`). For the mender it now means `model_catalog`'s `default=True` model for that runner's CLI (`model_catalog.py:246-254`: `claude-sonnet-5-5` for Claude Code), and the existing branch reuses or creates a runner for it (`stalls.py:422-439`). An explicitly chosen model is unchanged. No migration: :8000's entry (an Opus runner, no model) moves to Sonnet at the next wake after the restart. Rejected: writing Sonnet into existing rows, which is a data migration for a choice that resolving can express. The other Manager jobs keep 'empty means the runner's model'. The Manager page names the mender's default so the cost is visible before it runs.

Tier 1: no migration, no schema change. Hazards that remain are the ordinary ones for this repo: the UI bundle commit reaches :8000 on its next reload, and the `mcp_server.py` edit reaches agents at a Hub's next restart (`.claude/rules/mcp-server.md`). The operator authorised :8000 changes on 2026-10-27.

lifecycle: Tier 1 (change). A one-off change to the mender (`a-stalled-project-wakes-a-doctor-that-unblocks-it`) and to flow firing. After the build, reconcile the mender capability's 'ask-before-hardcore' and 'mender-is-a-run' requirements (ask with a note rather than wait; empty model means the catalog default) and set F1049's Status line in scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md.

open_questions.question: F1049's rule: decided as 'a completed task whose author's turn is still running is in flight', not 'seen on two consecutive firings'. It depends on the queue's state rather than on timing, and the turn's end already requests the firing that dispatches the review (design D1, D2).

'Sonnet by default' for a project that already has a mender runner: decided that an empty Manager model means the catalog default model of the runner's CLI, so :8000 moves to Sonnet at the next wake with no migration, and an explicitly chosen model is kept (design D5).

Questions 'while the operator is away': decided that the mender's questions are always notes, because no presence signal exists and a note costs at most one extra turn when the operator is present (design D3). The surface is the existing non-blocking question on the Overview's Needs you list.

On the operator's :8000 Hub the Manager's mender entry names claude-opus-5-5 explicitly (set 2026-10-23), so the default-model rule keeps Opus there. Decided 2026-10-27: when this slice ships, the orchestrator sets that entry's model to claude-sonnet-5-5 through the Manager settings (operator authorised changes to :8000).

problem: On the operator's :8000 Hub, during slice B's flow on the night of 2026-10-26/27 (22:57 to 05:44), the mender cost $15.9 API-equivalent over 42 Opus runs, 36% of the night's spend. Three things made it expensive. (1) All 6 `loop_stalled` stalls were false alarms of one shape (F1049, `scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md` line 40529): a task reached `completed`, `flow_advance` fired the flow 3 s later (`hub/hub/flow_advance.py:41`, `DEBOUNCE_SECONDS = 3.0`), the author's turn was still running so `decide_firing` deferred the review (`hub/hub/scheduler.py:2561-2570`), nothing else was claimable, and the firing reported 'loop queue is stalled' (`scheduler.py:4403-4412`). Each time the mender woke on Opus, found the review running, changed nothing and ended `fixed` (23:42, 23:53, 00:15, 04:20, 04:53, 05:24). (2) The mender ran on Opus because `ensure_mender` uses the chosen runner's model whenever the Manager entry names none (`hub/hub/stalls.py:417-439`). (3) It asked the operator 27 blocking questions, each a 4-minute wait (`hub/hub/api/v1/agents.py:1806`, `DEFAULT_QUESTION_WAIT_SECONDS = 240`) that ran out unanswered because the operator was asleep; its brief tells it to 'ask_user, and wait for the answer' (`stalls.py:636`). F1048 (a given-up stall re-raised every 5 minutes, 30 of 40 stalls) and F1050 are fixed already (c6cc29d) and are not part of this change.

requirements.rationale: F1049: six Opus mender turns in one night, each finding a review that was about to start. The author's run ending is what makes the work reviewable and already requests the next firing (`flow_advance.after_run`), so this is the flow working, not a stall.
requirements.statement: A flow firing that finds a `completed` task whose completing agent still has a run `running` on that task records no `loop_stalled` stall, briefs no mender, writes no `skipped` job run, and its decision carries no stall reason, whether or not other tasks of the flow are gated on that task's approval.

requirements.rationale: Requirement hand-off-gap-is-not-a-stall is safe only because this firing exists; the acceptance drive asserts both halves so neither can regress alone.
requirements.statement: When the completing agent's run on that task ends, the firing its end requests selects the task for review by a reviewer other than its author, without waiting for the flow's cron tick.

requirements.rationale: The fix narrows what counts as a stall; it must not delay a real one.
requirements.statement: A flow firing that finds open work, nothing claimable, and no agent's run `running` on any of the flow's tasks records a `loop_stalled` stall on that first firing and wakes the enabled mender once, as today.

requirements.rationale: Treating the task as in flight removes the firing's stall; the sweep is what keeps a run that never ends from hiding forever.
requirements.statement: A completed task held in flight by its author's run is still reported by the stall sweep when that run is recorded `running` but this Hub is not executing it (`dead_run`), and when its loop has had no run started and no task moved for `NO_PROGRESS_MINUTES` (`no_progress`).

requirements.rationale: On :8000 the operator chose a runner, not a model, and got Opus for 42 turns. Mending is reading state and calling a few routes; the everyday model is enough, and an operator who wants more can choose it.
requirements.statement: When the project's Manager mender entry names no model, every mender turn runs on the model the model catalog marks `default` for the CLI of the entry's runner (`claude-sonnet-5-5` for Claude Code), whatever model that runner itself names; a project whose entry already names no model moves to it at the mender's next wake, with no migration.
A model the operator chose for the mender on the Manager page is the model its turns run on, as today.

requirements.rationale: Warn, don't gate: the operator must be able to see what the mender costs before it runs.
requirements.statement: The Manager page's model menu for the mender, with no model chosen, names the model the mender will run on (for a Claude Code runner: 'Sonnet 5.5 (the mender's default)'), never 'The runner's model'; the other jobs' menus are unchanged.

requirements.rationale: 27 four-minute waits ran out unanswered on 2026-10-26/27. A wait on a person who is asleep only ends in 'nobody responded'.
requirements.statement: Every question the Hub's mender asks through `ask_user` is recorded with `blocking` false and no `wait_expires_at`, whatever `blocking` value it passed; the call returns without waiting; it parks no task; and a blocking question from any other agent still waits as today.

requirements.rationale: Keeps the rule that the hardcore moves wait for the operator, without a wait; F1048's rule then keeps the stall the operator's while its reason holds, so the note is not asked again.
requirements.statement: The mender's brief tells it that, for each action it must ask the operator about, it leaves the question as a note, does not take the action, and ends the stall with `mend_end_stall(stall_id, "gave_up", summary)` whose summary names the note.

requirements.rationale: The mender holds one open conversation per stall; delivering into the latest open one (`questions.py:164`) would wake it in another stall's thread.
requirements.statement: Answering (or declining) a question that no run is waiting on delivers the answer as a new queued turn into the conversation the question was asked from when that conversation is still open, and into the asker's latest open conversation only when it is not.

requirements.rationale: Today every non-blocking question whose run ended reads 'nobody is waiting on this answer any more' (`OverviewScreen.tsx:117`), which is false for a note whose answer is delivered.
requirements.statement: The Overview's Needs-you list shows each unanswered mender note with its question, an action that opens the conversation it was asked in, and no sentence saying nobody is waiting on the answer; the 'nobody is waiting' sentence is shown only for a blocking question whose asking turn has ended.

in_scope: `decide_firing`'s fresh-review arm: a completed task whose completing agent's turn on it is still running is recorded in flight (held by that agent), not deferred, so the firing is not a stall.
The mender's model: an empty Manager model means the catalog default model of the runner's CLI; the Manager page shows that default.

The mender's questions: recorded as notes Hub-side whatever `blocking` it passes; `ask_user` returns at once when the Hub recorded none of the batch as blocking; the mender's brief says to leave a note, not act, and end `gave_up` naming it.
An answer to a question is delivered into the conversation the question was asked from when that conversation is still open (else the latest open one, as today).
The Overview's Needs-you row for a note: no 'nobody is waiting' sentence on a non-blocking question, and its action opens the thread it was asked in.
non_goals: F1048 (a given-up stall re-raised) and F1050 (a stuck_task stall for a deleted task): fixed in c6cc29d. F1047 (input in an archived conversation): fixed in 5b40da0.
An operator-presence or 'away' signal. None exists today and this change does not add one: the mender's questions are notes always (design D3).
Blocking questions from any agent other than the Hub's mender: their waits, deadlines and task parking are unchanged.
A confirmation delay (seeing a stall on two consecutive firings) for any stall cause: rejected in design D1.
Choosing the mender's model per stall cause, or escalating to a larger model when it gives up.
Slice L's check ordering, slice M's automatic override and fix task, slice D's driver/level/people and window: N changes only when the mender is woken, what it runs on and how it asks.
A new stall outcome such as 'asked': a note ends the stall `gave_up`, which F1048's rule already keeps the operator's while its reason holds.

summary: Three changes to the Hub's mender, all from the night of 2026-10-26/27. First, a flow firing that finds a completed task whose author's turn is still running treats that task as in flight, so the seconds between a task's completion and its review dispatch are no longer recorded as a `loop_stalled` stall that wakes the mender (F1049). The rule is a fact about the queue, not a timer: the author's run ending already requests the firing that dispatches the review (`flow_advance.after_run`). Second, when the Manager's mender entry names no model, the mender runs on the default model the catalog declares for its runner's CLI (Sonnet 5.5 for Claude Code) instead of whatever model the chosen runner names, and the Manager page says so. Third, every question the mender asks is recorded as a note: nobody waits on it, no 4-minute wait runs out, the mender takes no action that needed the answer and ends its stall `gave_up` naming the note, and the operator's answer, whenever it comes, wakes the mender in the thread it was asked from.
